title: The last post and the child outside the city
subtitle: In which an army turns a page, a ship burns late, and the tap still will not turn.
lede: The thirtieth of September 2026 lifts a gate in Baghdad and does not let a child rise in the province around Kyiv.

body:
There are mornings when an army turns a page and believes the chapter is finished, while a child outside a capital does not get up and a ship admits only a day later that it burned. The thirtieth of September 2026 is such a morning: Baghdad declares four holidays, Hormuz sends a warning that arrives late, and the field in the east keeps writing a list that does not keep holidays.

I. The last post

By Wednesday the last American soldiers are meant to have left their bases in Iraq — Erbil in the north, the edge of Baghdad’s airport, what still held of the Green Zone. It is the second complete departure after 2011, and this time it carries the date of a 2024 agreement that Joe Biden signed and Donald Trump has now run to its end, even as the same Trump wages war on the Gulf. About twenty-five hundred troops stood there in recent years. More than forty-five hundred Americans have died in this country since 2003. 1 2

Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi calls the first of October a new day of Iraqi statehood and orders four official holidays. The disarmament of Iran-aligned militias has been pushed to the end of June 2027. Tehran speaks of a victory for the axis. Iraqi security officials speak of room the Islamic State might use again. 3 4 16

An army leaves because a calendar says so. The neighbours who stay have no calendar for influence.

Operation Inherent Resolve ends on the day the Iran war still holds the needle’s eye shut. Anyone who reads the pullout only as Iraqi sovereignty reads half. Anyone who reads it only as a gift to Tehran reads half as well.

II. The fire that arrives late

The British maritime watch reports on Tuesday, after a delay, a ship in the Strait of Hormuz struck by a projectile of unclear origin, fire out, crew safe, under way again. Iran had spoken of nineteen vessels. Evidence for the nineteen is missing. The one late hit stands. 5 6

Abbas Araghchi had expected a formal American answer to the seven-day plan still on Tuesday. By Wednesday morning the expectation has become neither a date nor a clause. Ship counters speak of oil flows back toward four fifths of the pre-war mark. The tap stands. 7 18

III. The child outside the city

On the night into Tuesday Moscow sends a Zircon or Oniks, two ballistic missiles and one hundred and fifty-two drones. Ukraine’s air force says all three missiles were brought down, and one hundred and six drones with them. Under the rubble of the Academy rescuers find a second dead. 8 9 11

Zelensky thanks the United States and Norway for a NASAMS system. Early Wednesday a strike in Kyiv region kills a child. Five more people are wounded. 10 12

IV. The list that knows side doors

Since one minute past midnight the northern ban has held. Crown Royal may send whisky in bulk. Labatt fills part of its beer in American halls. The small stills do not have that sentence. 13

V. At the edge of the page

King Mohammed VI names Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri Morocco’s first woman prime minister. Puntland’s maritime police free the tanker Honour 25. In Jalud settlers attack a village. 14 15 17

The chronicler’s close

The last post in Iraq is a date and a vacuum at once. The field has a child outside Kyiv and three intercepted missiles that do not fill the next magazine. The tap has a late flame and no clause. The customs list knows side doors for those who keep two addresses.

What stays open is Hormuz, the eastern field, the northern list and the empty yard on the Tigris. The two thrones and the hall of nations have lain still for three days; the book proposes to close them until a sentence falls that is more than the memory of a carpet.

Today the book does not keep a finger in an old crease. It lays a sheet on the last post and on the child outside the city and watches what the first of October will make of a holiday and of a siren.
